## Brief description

*The 100* is a post-apocalyptic science fiction drama that premiered on The CW in 2014.
The show follows young survivors sent from a space habitat back to Earth to test whether the planet is habitable again.

![The 100 title card](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/7/73/The_100_title_card.jpg)

Source: [Wikipedia — *The 100*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_100_(TV_series))

## Viewership data used in this report

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r data}
viewership <- data.frame(
  season = 1:7,
  avg_viewers_millions = c(2.69, 1.81, 1.58, 0.95, 0.87, 0.76, 0.58)
)

viewership
```

Source: [Wikipedia — List of *The 100* episodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_100_episodes)

## Basic statistics

```{r stats}
summary_stats <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Maximum average season viewership (M)",
             "Minimum average season viewership (M)",
             "Mean average season viewership (M)",
             "Total drop from Season 1 to Season 7 (M)"),
  value = c(
    max(viewership$avg_viewers_millions),
    min(viewership$avg_viewers_millions),
    round(mean(viewership$avg_viewers_millions), 2),
    round(viewership$avg_viewers_millions[1] - tail(viewership$avg_viewers_millions, 1), 2)
  )
)

summary_stats
```

## Graph: Viewership over time

```{r plot-trend, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
plot(
  viewership$season,
  viewership$avg_viewers_millions,
  type = "b",
  pch = 19,
  lwd = 2,
  col = "#1f77b4",
  xlab = "Season",
  ylab = "Average viewers (millions)",
  main = "The 100: Average season viewership"
)
grid()
```

## Graph: Season-to-season changes

```{r plot-delta, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
season_change <- diff(viewership$avg_viewers_millions)
bar_cols <- ifelse(season_change < 0, "#d62728", "#2ca02c")

barplot(
  season_change,
  names.arg = paste0("S", 1:6, "→S", 2:7),
  col = bar_cols,
  border = NA,
  ylab = "Change in average viewers (millions)",
  main = "Season-to-season change in average viewership"
)
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```

## Observed changes

**AI-generated section (manually verified):**
The overall trend is a steady decrease in average season viewership. For example, average viewership decreased by **`r round(viewership$avg_viewers_millions[3] - viewership$avg_viewers_millions[5], 2)` million** between Season 3 and Season 5 (from **`r viewership$avg_viewers_millions[3]`M** to **`r viewership$avg_viewers_millions[5]`M**), which is about **`r round((viewership$avg_viewers_millions[3] - viewership$avg_viewers_millions[5]) / viewership$avg_viewers_millions[3] * 100, 1)`%**.

A larger decline is visible from Season 1 to Season 4, followed by smaller declines in later seasons.
